headline: Google extends Gemini chat retention, eases AI training opt-out
summary: Google is separating AI-training and chat-history toggles in Gemini's activity settings, making it easier to opt out of having chats used for AI training while still keeping chat history. At the same time, Google is extending how long it retains Gemini chats, from 72 hours to two months, even for users with history off, rolling out globally over coming weeks.

claims.statement: AI training and chat history will now have separate toggles in Gemini's activity settings.

sources.quote: AI training and chat history will now have separate toggles in the Gemini activity settings.

claims.statement: Google is extending Gemini data retention from 72 hours to two months.

sources.quote: From 72 hours to 2 months in a single quiet announcement.

claims.statement: Users will soon be able to turn off Gemini model training while still retaining access to previous chats.

sources.quote: You’ll soon be able to turn off Gemini model training but still retain access to your previous chats with Google’s AI.

claims.statement: The chat-retention extension will roll out globally over the coming weeks.

sources.quote: Google's Gemini update extending chat retention will roll out globally over the coming weeks.

discrepancies.explanation: One outlet frames the change as giving users more control to opt out of AI training, while another frames it as Google retaining data for longer even when users ask it not to.

quotes.quote: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
Careful what you ask Google's AI, because it's storing it even if you ask it not to
